detail.longDescription: A "still" can't do this. AI "still" can't do that. That "still" is doing a lot of work there. Most white collar jobs will be gone in a few years, starting from programmers. "BuT I aM aN EnGinEeR", yeah dude. "We are greatful for what you did so far." will be what you'll hear before getting laid off. Just look at 2 years ago, remember the times you were making fun of stupid ChatGPT responses. That changed dramatically. What do you think will happen in 2 years ? Software development will basically become a dark factory overseen by a few engineers. There won't be simply enough of a market to employ that many engineers. "Ok, let's build a product", I hear you mumbling. Any technical product will be eaten by giants. Oh, you are making X for Y ? Yeah in 2 years, that will be a single prompt. These are thoughts I have been having lately. I got laid off a week ago. I am one of the people who being a software developer is part of their identity. I can find a job, that's not really my worry, I have enough reference and experience ( 8 years, full stack and mobile as well ) to get into a job. But honestly I don't want to apply for a role that won't exist in 3 years. I want to play my cards right. What do you think I should do ? I need help.
